sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface vs. total CB2 expression quantified by thrombin cleavage of surface HA epitopes prior to fixation; surface display confirmed. Construct used in pharmacological surface-display assays.
sites.rationale: CB2 has no signal peptide; the topology landmarks place residues 1–34 as extracellular, making the N-terminus the sole extracellular terminus. The paper states the HA tag is 'appended at the N-terminus' of full-length, membrane-anchored hCB2 but names no specific residue number, so the junction is topology-derived as insert_after_residue=0 (prepend before M1). L2 independently confirms the tag is surface-accessible via thrombin cleavage, validating surface display. No signal peptide is present to cleave the tag off. Full-length human CB2 (hCB2 wt) with an HA tag and three thrombin cleavage sites appended at the N-terminus, assembled by overlap-extension PCR and ligated into pcDNA5/FRT; used in surface-display assays in transfected cells.

sites.evidence_type: published tolerance of a different insertion (transposon, FP fusion)
sites.functional_impact_measured: Live-cell surface labeling confirmed at the plasma membrane. Signaling and trafficking assessed: 'little impact on CB signaling and trafficking' (L5); 'without disrupting CB signaling or trafficking' (L3).
sites.rationale: L4 explicitly names 'CB2-S29' as the construct used for live-cell imaging, pinning the modification to residue S29. Python verification confirms seq[28]='S', placing S29 within the extracellular N-terminal domain (EC 1–34) and 6 residues from the TM1 boundary (35), well above the ≥3-residue minimum. The ncAA substitution at S29 is a different modality from a sequence-inserted epitope tag, so evidence_type is 'published tolerance of a different insertion'; cited_tag_residue=29. L3 and L5 corroborate that this labeling approach preserves CB2R signaling and trafficking. CB2-S29 construct: TCO*A non-canonical amino acid incorporated at position S29 of full-length CB2R in live cells; fluorophore attached via copper-free click chemistry for live-cell surface imaging alongside R-GECO calcium reporter.

literature_notes: Two ledger-supported sites identified, both in the extracellular N-terminal domain (EC 1–34). L1/L2 ground the N-terminal prepend (insert_after_residue=0) via an HA+3TCS tag on full-length membrane-anchored hCB2, with surface display confirmed by thrombin cleavage. L4 (supported by L3/L5) grounds a validated site at residue S29 via ncAA (TCO*A) incorporation and click-chemistry fluorophore attachment, with signaling and trafficking preserved. No ledger evidence supports any of the three short extracellular loops (ECL1: 93–104, ECL2: 173–189, ECL3: 267–279) for tag insertion in CB2. ECL2 (173–189) contains three cysteines (C174, C175, C179) likely involved in disulfide bonds, making it a poor candidate regardless. No intracellular or function-abrogating positions were reported in the ledger for CB2.
